the fluoride ion can be encapsulated within an octasilsesquisoxane cage, that it is relatively straightforward, although not always straightforward, to prepare these compounds and that they have been characterized by a range of techniques.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of a new class of fluoride-encapulated octasilsessquioxane cage compound.
the development of new synthetic routes to prepare a variety of fluoride encapsulated silsesquioxanes, and to understand their structure and reactivity.
the preparation of a range of fluoride- and other anion-encapsulated cage compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the TBAF approach to encapsulation is a very useful synthetic tool that can be applied to a range of substrates and that the encapsulated fluoride ion can be readily removed from the encapsulating cage by reaction with a Lewis acid.
the fluoride-encapsulating cage is a robust entity, which can survive a range of conditions and can be readily prepared in high yields.
the TBAF method of fluoride encapsulation in octasilsessquioxane cages is a very versatile method of encapsulating a range of anions in a range of silsesquioxanes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the encapsulated anion is not fixed within the cage, but can move in and out of it.

the TBAF method of encapsulating fluoride ions in octasilsquioxane cages is very effective for a wide range of aryl or vinyl groups but the corresponding sp(2) carbon derivatives are much more difficult to prepare.
whilst fluoride ion entrapments within octasilsesquisoxane cages are relatively straightforward to achieve, it is more challenging to achieve the same with other anions.

the fluoride-encapsulating TBAF route is a viable synthetic route to a variety of fluoride-encapsulation octasilsesqiuoxane cages and the resulting compounds are stable and can be handled in air.
